\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بسته} \fa{به} (baste be)}{بسته به (baste be)}]{\fa{بسته} \fa{به} (baste be) — depending on}

\label{lesson:FA-C395-baste-be}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a risk, then the Persian for to take a risk.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بسته} \fa{به}}
\textbf{\fa{بسته} \fa{به}} (\emph{baste be}) — \textquotedblleft{}depending on\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قیمت} \fa{بسته} \fa{به} \fa{فصل} \fa{فرق} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qeymat baste be fasl farq mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The price varies depending on the season.
\end{quote}

\emph{Baste} \textquotedblleft{}bound\textquotedblright{} + \emph{be} \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{}. It takes a noun or a clause: \emph{baste be inke} … .

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{بسته} \fa{به}} is native Persian, literally \textquotedblleft{}bound to\textquotedblright{}: \emph{baste} is the participle of \emph{bastan} \textquotedblleft{}to bind\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB traces to PIE \emph{b\textsuperscript{h}end\textsuperscript{h}-} \textquotedblleft{}to bind\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baste be}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baste be}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{baste be}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a risk, then the Persian for to take a risk, then say \emph{baste be} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{وابسته} (vâbaste)}{وابسته (vâbaste)}]{\fa{وابسته} (vâbaste) — dependent; attached}

\label{lesson:FA-C395-vabaste}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to take a risk, then the Persian for depending on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{وابسته}}
\textbf{\fa{وابسته}} (\emph{vâbaste}) — \textquotedblleft{}dependent; attached\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{هنوز} \fa{از} \fa{نظر} \fa{مالی} \fa{به} \fa{پدرش} \fa{وابسته} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u hanuz az nazar-e mâli be pedarash vâbaste ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He still depends on his father for money.
\end{quote}

\emph{Vâbaste be} — dependent on. Also emotionally attached to someone.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{وابسته}} is native Persian, built from the prefix \emph{vâ-} + \emph{baste} \textquotedblleft{}bound\textquotedblright{}, the participle of \emph{bastan} \textquotedblleft{}to bind\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB traces it to PIE \emph{b\textsuperscript{h}end\textsuperscript{h}-}). To depend is to be tied to something.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vâbaste}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vâbaste}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{vâbaste}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to take a risk, then the Persian for depending on, then say \emph{vâbaste} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{وابسته} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Dependent; attached\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شرایط} (sharâyet)}{شرایط (sharâyet)}]{\fa{شرایط} (sharâyet) — conditions, circumstances}

\label{lesson:FA-C395-sharayet}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for depending on, then the Persian for dependent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شرایط}}
\textbf{\fa{شرایط}} (\emph{sharâyet}) — \textquotedblleft{}conditions, circumstances\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{این} \fa{شرایط} \fa{نمیتوانیم} \fa{سفر} \fa{کنیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dar in sharâyet nemitavânim safar konim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In these circumstances we cannot travel.
\end{quote}

An Arabic broken plural of \emph{shart} \textquotedblleft{}condition\textquotedblright{}. It also means terms: \emph{sharâyet-e qarârdâd}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{شرایط}} is an Arabic broken plural of \emph{shart}, which was borrowed from Arabic \emph{sharṭ} \textquotedblleft{}condition\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for depending on, then the Persian for dependent, then say \emph{sharâyet} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{به} \fa{محض} \fa{اینکه} (be mahz-e inke)}{به محض اینکه (be mahz-e inke)}]{\fa{به} \fa{محض} \fa{اینکه} (be mahz-e inke) — as soon as}

\label{lesson:FA-C395-be-mahz-e-inke}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for dependent, then the Persian for conditions.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{به} \fa{محض} \fa{اینکه}}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{محض} \fa{اینکه}} (\emph{be mahz-e inke}) — \textquotedblleft{}as soon as\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{به} \fa{محض} \fa{اینکه} \fa{رسیدم،} \fa{به} \fa{تو} \fa{زنگ} \fa{میزنم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{be mahz-e inke residam, be to zang mizanam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
As soon as I arrive, I will call you.
\end{quote}

It takes the past even for a future event: \emph{be mahz-e inke residam} — as soon as I arrive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{محض} \fa{اینکه}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}at the mere fact that\textquotedblright{}: \emph{mahz} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{maḥḍ} \textquotedblleft{}pure, mere\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{be} and \emph{inke} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{} are Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be mahz-e inke}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{be mahz-e inke}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for dependent, then the Persian for conditions, then say \emph{be mahz-e inke} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تا} \fa{زمانی} \fa{که} (tâ zamâni ke)}{تا زمانی که (tâ zamâni ke)}]{\fa{تا} \fa{زمانی} \fa{که} (tâ zamâni ke) — as long as; until}

\label{lesson:FA-C395-ta-zamani-ke}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for conditions, then the Persian for as soon as.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تا} \fa{زمانی} \fa{که}}
\textbf{\fa{تا} \fa{زمانی} \fa{که}} (\emph{tâ zamâni ke}) — \textquotedblleft{}as long as; until\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تا} \fa{زمانی} \fa{که} \fa{اینجا} \fa{هستی،} \fa{میتوانی} \fa{از} \fa{اتاق} \fa{من} \fa{استفاده} \fa{کنی}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tâ zamâni ke injâ hasti, mitavâni az otâq-e man estefâde koni.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
As long as you are here, you can use my room.
\end{quote}

With a negative verb it means \textquotedblleft{}until\textquotedblright{}: \emph{tâ zamâni ke nayâyad} — until he comes.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{تا} \fa{زمانی} \fa{که}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}until the time that\textquotedblright{}: \emph{tâ} is inherited Persian (EtymDB traces it to Middle Persian \textquotedblleft{}until, so that\textquotedblright{}), and \emph{zamân} comes from Arabic \emph{zamān} \textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
